prompt.en: "We have become among our people like the Children of Israel among Pharaoh's folk: they slaughter our sons and spare our women." Who said this?

explanation.en: Speaking to al-Minhal, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn likened the Household's plight to the Children of Israel under Pharaoh, whose sons were slaughtered and women spared, saying the family is granted no right.

anchor.quote: We have become among our people like the Children of Israel among Pharaoh's folk: they slaughter our sons and spare our women

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, why does Shia exegesis argue that verses 5 and 6 are not about Moses?

options.en: The plural 'from them' would otherwise read 'from him'
Moses was an apostle, not one of the imams
The abased in the verse are Pharaoh's people, not Israel
The promise was revealed in Mecca, long after Moses

explanation.en: Al-Qummi reasons that the verse says 'from them' in the plural, not 'from him,' so it cannot be about Moses alone but concerns the Family of Muhammad.

anchor.quote: the plural 'from them' shows the verse is not about Moses, since that would read 'from him'

prompt.en: According to the narration on verse 7, everyone who saw Moses was moved to love him.

explanation.en: The narration says no one saw Moses without loving him, citing God's words 'I cast upon you love from Me,' so it is true that all who saw him loved him.

anchor.quote: No one saw Moses without loving him; that is God's saying, 'I cast upon you love from Me.'

prompt.en: Al-Tusi explains that this revelation was ____ cast into her heart, not prophecy.

explanation.en: Al-Tusi reads the revelation to Moses' mother as inspiration cast into her heart, not prophecy, so she received it without being made a prophet.

anchor.quote: Al-Tusi explains that this revelation was inspiration cast into her heart, not prophecy

prompt.en: According to the essay, how does al-Tusi explain why the infant refused every nurse's milk?

options.en: As a legal ban forbidding him to be nursed
As God turning the child away from them, not a ban
As an illness that kept him from feeding
As the infant's grief at being taken from his mother

explanation.en: The essay says al-Tusi reads the refused milk not as a legal ban but as God turning the child away from the nurses, so his sister could guide them to his own mother.

anchor.quote: the milk of every nurse is refused, which al-Tusi explains as God turning the child away from them rather than any legal ban

prompt.en: His coming of age was eighteen years, and 'became fully matured' means that he ____.

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq glosses 'became fully matured' as Moses growing a beard, the mark of full physical maturity, which the narration sets apart from his coming of age at eighteen years.

anchor.quote: His coming of age was eighteen years, and 'became fully matured' means that he grew a beard.

prompt.en: According to the essay, who were the two men Moses came upon fighting in the city?

options.en: Two Copts quarreling in Pharaoh's household
Two Israelites disputing over their inheritance
An Israelite of his own people and a Copt, his enemy
A Copt and a traveler from Midian

explanation.en: The essay identifies the pair as an Israelite of Moses's own people and a Copt who was his enemy, with the Israelite calling on Moses for help against the Copt.

anchor.quote: He comes upon two men fighting, one an Israelite of his own people and the other a Copt, his enemy

prompt.en: "May this name bring you joy - the Shia. Have you not heard God say, 'The one who was from his followers sought his help against him who was from his enemies'?" Who said this?

explanation.en: Speaking to Abu Basir, Imam al-Sadiq took the verse's phrase 'his followers' as naming the Shia, telling him that the name should bring him joy.

anchor.quote: May this name bring you joy - the Shia. Have you not heard God say, 'The one who was from his followers sought his help against him who was from his enemies'?

prompt.en: According to the passage, one reading holds that Moses striking down the Copt was not evil. On what ground?

options.en: The Copt had struck Moses first, so it was self-defense
God had commanded the killing; only its delay would have been better
The Copt stood condemned to death under Egyptian law
Moses acted to protect a fellow prophet from harm

explanation.en: One reading holds the act was not evil because God had commanded the killing; only delaying it would have been better, so no sin attached to Moses.

anchor.quote: al-Tusi reports that his companions hold the act was not evil at all: God had commanded the killing, and only its delay would have been better

prompt.en: According to the essay, Moses leaves the city reassured and safe, no longer in danger from the chiefs.

explanation.en: The essay says Moses departs fearful and vigilant, and that the passage leaves him a fugitive, thrown wholly on his Lord, on the road that will take him to Midian.

anchor.quote: The passage leaves him a fugitive, thrown wholly on his Lord, on the road that will take him to Midian

prompt.en: According to the passage, Moses set out for Midian even though he did not know the way there.

explanation.en: The essay says Moses turned toward Midian hoping his Lord would show him the right way, even though, as the commentary notes, he did not actually know the road there.

anchor.quote: though al-Mizan notes he did not know the road there

prompt.en: "By God, he asked God for nothing but bread to eat, for he used to eat the herbs of the earth." Who said this about Moses?

explanation.en: Imam Ali swore that Moses begged God only for bread, saying he lived on the herbs of the earth, so thin that the green showed through his belly.

anchor.quote: By God, he asked God for nothing but bread to eat, for he used to eat the herbs of the earth

prompt.en: In the narration on verse 26, how did the daughter learn that Moses was trustworthy?

options.en: He drove the other shepherds away from the well
He refused to take any wages for the watering
He told her to walk behind him, not looking at women
He carried water for her aged father himself

explanation.en: The daughter said she walked ahead until Moses told her to walk behind him and guide him if he strayed, for his people do not look at women's backs.

anchor.quote: I walked ahead of him, and he said, walk behind me, and if I go astray, guide me to the road; I am of a people who do not look at women's backs

prompt.en: Moses accepts, keeping either term ____ to himself, and calls God witness over what they agree.

explanation.en: The essay reads verse 28 as Moses accepting the pact while keeping the choice of which term to complete open to himself, calling God witness to their agreement.

anchor.quote: Moses accepts, keeping either term open to himself, and calls God witness over what they agree

prompt.en: According to the passage, what does the Quran's own account say about the identity of the man who hosted Moses?

options.en: It names him directly as the prophet Shu'ayb
It calls him a believer from Pharaoh's people
It lists him among the messengers sent to Midian
It does not name the man at all

explanation.en: The perspectives open by noting the Quran does not name Moses' host; that silence is why Shia narrations and Sunni scholars discuss his identity at all.

anchor.quote: The Quran does not name the man who hosted Moses.

prompt.en: According to the passage, what does the context show about the moment Moses saw the fire on the mountain?

options.en: It was night, bitterly cold, and they had lost their way
It was a bright, warm morning on the road
They were resting by a well outside a town
A crowd of travellers was gathered at the fire

explanation.en: The passage says the context shows it was night, bitterly cold, and that Moses and his family had lost their way when he saw the fire on the mountain.

anchor.quote: the context shows it was night, bitterly cold, and that they had lost their way when he saw a fire on the side of the mountain

prompt.en: "The right bank of the valley is the Euphrates, the blessed spot is Karbala, and the tree is Muhammad." Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked about the right bank, the blessed spot and the tree, Imam al-Sadiq identified them as the Euphrates, Karbala, and Muhammad and his family.

anchor.quote: The right bank of the valley that God mentioned in His Book is the Euphrates; the blessed spot is Karbala; and the tree is Muhammad

prompt.en: The hand emerging 'white, without any fault' means its whiteness was not the whiteness of ____.

explanation.en: The note explains that the hand coming out 'white, without any fault' means its whiteness was not the whiteness of leprosy.

anchor.quote: The hand emerging 'white, without any fault' means its whiteness was not the whiteness of leprosy

prompt.en: In a narration here, to what does the Prophet liken God strengthening his own arm by Ali?

options.en: To God strengthening Adam by the angels
To God strengthening Moses' arm by Aaron
To God strengthening Abraham by Ishmael
To God strengthening David by Solomon

explanation.en: The report likens God strengthening the Prophet's arm by Ali to God strengthening Moses' arm by his brother Aaron, matching Moses' request for Aaron as a helper.

anchor.quote: one by whom Allah strengthened my arm as He strengthened Moses' arm by Aaron

prompt.en: In the Shia reading, 'leaders who invite to the Fire' and 'leaders guiding by Our command' name one and the same class of leader.

explanation.en: False: the Shia reading sets the two verses against each other to mark two opposed classes of leader, those who put God's command before their own and those who put their own before His Book.

anchor.quote: to mark two opposed classes of leader, those who put God's command before their own and those who put their own command and desires before His Book

prompt.en: "God has destroyed no people, no generation, no nation, no townsfolk with a punishment from heaven since the Torah was sent down upon the earth, except the townsfolk who were transformed into apes." Who said this?

explanation.en: The Prophet declared that since the Torah came down, no people have been destroyed by a punishment from heaven, except the townsfolk who were turned into apes.

anchor.quote: since the Torah was sent down upon the earth, except the townsfolk who were transformed into apes

prompt.en: According to the essay, why does Tabatabai say God recounted Moses' story to the Prophet, who witnessed none of it?

Because the former generations had all been destroyed
So the People of the Book would confirm the Quran
Because the Meccans demanded a Book like Moses'

explanation.en: The essay says the Prophet witnessed none of these events, yet God recounted them to him as a mercy, so he could warn a people no warner had reached before.

anchor.quote: the Prophet witnessed none of this, yet God recounted it to him as a mercy, so that he might warn a people who had received no earlier warner

prompt.en: According to a narration, God recorded on a leaf, two thousand years before creation, that He forgave the Shi'a of Muhammad's family before they sought forgiveness.

prompt.en: Al-Tusi finds in this the obligation of divine ____, for otherwise the verse would carry no sound meaning.

anchor.quote: Al-Tusi finds in this the obligation of divine grace, for otherwise the verse would carry no sound meaning

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, what do the Shia narrations and al-Razi both treat as the root of going astray?

anchor.quote: Both treat unguided personal opinion as the root of going astray, yet they differ on the missing guidance: an appointed Imam, or sound rational proof.
